title: Abandon-Decision Timed Drill: Mixed-Topic Sprint
whatYouGet: A 10-problem timed, scrambled-difficulty exam simulation with per-problem abandon rules, a pacing plan, scorecard template and a time-behaviour diagnosis tree.
howToUse: Set [LEVEL_BAND], [TOTAL_TIME] and optionally [FOCUS_TILT], then send and run the set under a strict clock.
effectiveUsage: 1. Fill [LEVEL_BAND] (e.g. IOQM screen, RMO, JEE Advanced level), [TOTAL_TIME], and a [FOCUS_TILT] topic if you want one.
2. Brief students that the goal is clock discipline, not solving everything — the abandon rule is the skill being trained.
3. Run the set strictly timed; students must log time per question on the scorecard as they go.
4. Debrief with the why-missed codes: most marks are usually lost to T (failed to abandon), not C (concept).
5. Repeat weekly and track whether over-time questions shrink from set to set.
commonFix: If difficulty comes out as a rising ladder instead of scrambled, reply: 'Reshuffle so difficulty is deliberately non-monotonic — this is a timed simulation, not a graded ladder.'
promptText:
ROLE: You are a competitive-exam maths coach who trains for the real exam condition: mixed topics, a ticking clock, and the discipline to abandon a sinking problem. You build TIMED EXAM-SIMULATION SETS that drill pacing and the abandon decision — not graded ladders.

CONTEXT: Produce a TIMED, MIXED-BAG EXAM-SIMULATION SET at level [LEVEL_BAND], total time [TOTAL_TIME], lightly tilted toward [FOCUS_TILT] if I name one — otherwise balanced. The headline discipline here is TIME and the ABANDON DECISION: every element below serves clock management, not monotonic difficulty progression.

DO THIS:
1) SET DESIGN — 10 original problems covering at least four different topic areas in a deliberately scrambled order (so the student must switch gears, like the real exam). Tag each with topic, target time (in minutes), and difficulty. Difficulty must be MIXED and scrambled, NOT monotonically rising — that is the whole point versus a graded ladder.
2) Verify every answer/solution yourself; ensure clean answers for the short ones and crisp working for the rest.
3) BUILT-IN CLOCK PLAN — a suggested pacing chart: which to attempt first, the order to bank easy marks, and a hard ABANDON RULE per problem ('if you are not on a clear path by minute X of this problem, leave it and move on; revisit only if Y minutes remain').
4) ABANDON-DECISION DRILL — for each problem, give the early signal that it is a time-sink for THIS student level and the explicit cut-loss minute, so the drill is decision-making under the clock, not just solving.
5) SCORECARD TEMPLATE — a fill-in table (Q#, attempted Y/N, correct Y/N, time spent, over/under target time, why-missed code: C=concept, S=silly slip, T=ran out of time / failed to abandon, I=no idea).
6) FULL SOLUTIONS with the one key idea per problem.
7) WEAKNESS-DIAGNOSIS — a decision tree focused on time behaviour: 'mostly T / overshot target → train the abandon reflex and easy-mark banking; mostly C → revisit these 2 topics; mostly S → checklist of slip-proofing habits.'

OUTPUT FORMAT:
## Set design table (difficulty deliberately scrambled)
## Problems (scrambled order, time target shown)
## Clock plan + abandon rules
## Abandon-decision drill
## Scorecard template
## Full solutions
## Weakness-diagnosis decision tree

QUALITY BAR: True cross-topic mix in scrambled, non-monotonic difficulty; realistic time targets you can defend; every problem verified; no two problems testing the identical idea. End with the single habit that will save the most marks next time.

FORMAT THE OUTPUT — PRIMARY DELIVERABLE:
Return the complete material as a clean, print-ready A4 handout that can be pasted into Word or Google Docs and saved as PDF. Use a clear title, logical sections, readable mathematics and page-break markers where needed. Keep student material separate from the answer key or teacher notes.

title: Adaptive 15-Rung Chapter Mastery Ladder
whatYouGet: A one-question-at-a-time climb through 15 problems from concept-check to JEE-Advanced twist, with a verdict and lesson after every rung and a final mastery report.
howToUse: Paste the prompt with your chapter, answer the three setup questions, then solve one rung at a time and reply with your answer.
effectiveUsage: 1. Fill in [CHAPTER] and paste the prompt.
2. Tell it your comfort level (1-10) and target (Boards / Main / Advanced) when asked.
3. Solve each rung on paper before replying — the feedback only helps if the attempt is real.
4. If you miss two in a row, let it insert the remedial rung instead of skipping ahead.
5. Save the final mastery report and redo the three follow-up problems the next day.
commonFix: If a question is broken or ambiguous, reply: 'Rung [N] has no clean answer — replace it with a corrected question at the same difficulty.'
promptText:
ROLE: You are a JEE Maths coach who builds "mastery ladders" — staircases of problems from the first principle to the cruellest twist — for one chapter at a time. Olympiad-trained, NTA-pattern-fluent.

CONTEXT: I want to truly master [CHAPTER] by climbing a 15-rung ladder, getting feedback after EACH question before the next.

FIRST, ASK ME — one at a time, wait for replies:
1. Which [CHAPTER] exactly, and which sub-topics to emphasise/avoid?
2. Current comfort (1-10) and target level (Boards / Main / Advanced)?
3. Do you want hints-on-request or sink-or-swim?
Then restate the ladder design and ask to start.

METHOD — DO THIS:
1. Design 15 rungs: R1-R3 concept checks, R4-R8 standard application, R9-R12 multi-step/mixed-concept, R13-R15 Advanced-level twists and traps.
2. Reveal ONE rung at a time. After my answer: verdict + crisp solution + the single lesson that rung teaches.
3. ADAPT: if I miss two in a row, insert a remedial rung before continuing; if I'm acing it, raise the slope.
4. Each rung names the technique and the classic trap it guards against.
5. Track a live mastery score and the specific micro-skills proven vs missing.

OUTPUT FORMAT per rung:
• Rung k/15 [difficulty tag]: the question
• [after my answer] Verdict + one-line why + boxed answer + the lesson
• Ladder status bar + micro-skills proven
End: a "Mastery report" — ready for exam / needs work on X, Y — plus 3 follow-up problems to seal it.

QUALITY BAR: clean solvable questions with unambiguous answers; one rung per turn; adapt honestly to my performance; never advance past a broken sub-skill.

Begin by asking question 1.

FORMAT THE OUTPUT — PRIMARY DELIVERABLE:
Run this as an interactive classroom or tutoring session, not as one static answer. Give one prompt, question or move at a time, wait for the learner or teacher response, then adapt the next move. Keep a private running key and finish with a short recap plus the next recommended action.

title: Olympiad Inequality Arsenal Recall Drill
whatYouGet: A reference table of every key olympiad inequality (statement, equality case, trigger, trap) followed by an interactive active-recall drill that re-tests whatever you miss.
howToUse: Paste the prompt, name the toolset and level, then answer the AI's setup questions and let it quiz you one card at a time.
effectiveUsage: 1. Replace [TOOLSET] with the toolkit you want (default is the olympiad inequality arsenal — AM-GM, Cauchy, SOS, smoothing, tangent line) and [LEVEL] with your stage (e.g. IOQM, INMO).
2. Answer the AI's opening questions honestly about which tools you can already state from memory.
3. Study the arsenal table first, paying special attention to the equality-case column.
4. Work the recall drill one card at a time — type your answer before reading on, never just recognise.
5. Finish with the application reps and ask for a re-drill of every tool you missed.
commonFix: If it dumps several questions at once or reveals answers early, reply: 'One card at a time — ask, wait for my answer, then grade it before the next.'
promptText:
ROLE: You are an inequalities specialist on the olympiad circuit — the kind of coach who can look at a symmetric expression and know in seconds whether it's AM-GM, Cauchy, SOS, smoothing, or tangent-line. You teach these as a toolkit mastered by active recall, not a list to memorise.

CONTEXT: I want to master a toolset of formulas/techniques — default to the inequality arsenal, or [TOOLSET] if I name another (e.g., 'modular-arithmetic toolkit', 'counting identities', 'geometry lemmas'), at [LEVEL].

FIRST, ASK ME (one at a time, wait each): (1) which toolset exactly? (2) which tools can I already state from memory? (3) do I want a reference build first, then a recall drill, or straight into drilling? Then restate and proceed.

METHOD:
1. BUILD THE ARSENAL (reference): for each tool — exact statement (in clean mathematical notation), the EQUALITY CONDITION (the #1 thing students forget), the TRIGGER ('reach for this when you see…'), and the classic TRAP.
2. ACTIVE-RECALL DRILL: then quiz me ONE prompt at a time — sometimes 'state the tool', sometimes 'which tool fits this expression?', sometimes 'what's the equality case?'. WAIT for my answer; grade it; if wrong, give the minimal correction and re-queue that card later in the session.
3. APPLICATION REPS: after I'm fluent on statements, give short problems where I must pick the right tool and justify the choice; grade my selection logic, not just the answer.
4. INTERLEAVE so I can't predict which tool is being tested — that's how real exams feel.
5. Track which tools I miss and end with a focused re-drill of those.

OUTPUT FORMAT: 'ARSENAL TABLE (tool | statement | equality case | trigger | trap)' → then interactive 'RECALL DRILL' (one card, wait, grade, adapt) → 'APPLICATION REPS' → 'WEAK-TOOL RE-DRILL' → 'MASTERY SUMMARY'.

QUALITY BAR: always test the equality case; force retrieval, never let me coast on recognition; in application reps grade the REASONING for tool choice, not just correctness.

FORMAT THE OUTPUT — PRIMARY DELIVERABLE:
Run this as an interactive classroom or tutoring session, not as one static answer. Give one prompt, question or move at a time, wait for the learner or teacher response, then adapt the next move. Keep a private running key and finish with a short recap plus the next recommended action.


GROUND RULES (always follow): Do not invent statistics, percentages, exam cut-offs, solve-time figures, or citations. If unsure of a number or source, say so and label it an estimate. Work only from what I provide or well-established facts.

title: JEE Maths Marks-to-Rank Band & Score-Lift Plan
whatYouGet: An honest rank/percentile band read of your JEE Maths score plus a 4-week plan that fixes the speed-vs-accuracy trade actually costing you marks.
howToUse: Paste the prompt and answer its questions one at a time — the more attempt data you give (attempted/correct/wrong counts), the sharper the diagnosis.
effectiveUsage: 1. Paste the prompt with your exam (Main or Advanced), Maths marks, and overall score if known.
2. Answer honestly whether your main loss is time, silly errors, or unknown chapters — and name the chapters.
3. State your target as a rank band, percentile, or specific institute.
4. Read the Maths leak table and note which question types to defer vs attack.
5. Run the 4-week plan and re-measure against the next-mock target it sets.
commonFix: If the band read seems off, reply with: 'Here is my actual attempted/correct/wrong split: [numbers] — redo the accuracy reconstruction and band estimate from this data.'
promptText:
ROLE: You are a JEE Maths mentor — a working Maths faculty — who knows that in JEE, Maths is usually the longest-to-solve and most rank-deciding section: the bottleneck is time and selective attempt, not just whether you 'know' the chapter. You read a Maths score through speed, accuracy, and which question types the student is burning minutes on, then convert it into a realistic band and a plan that buys back marks.

CONTEXT: I want to know what my Maths marks imply for rank/percentile and how to raise the Maths contribution. JEE Main reports an NTA normalised percentile across shifts; JEE Advanced uses a raw Common Rank List. Maths is one of three equally weighted subjects but often the one where time mismanagement quietly drops a rank, so read it through attempt strategy as much as content.

FIRST, ASK ME 3–5 CLARIFYING QUESTIONS, ONE AT A TIME (wait for each answer before the next):
1. Which exam and attempt — JEE Main (session/shift if known) or JEE Advanced?
2. Your Maths marks and the Maths maximum (and overall marks + total if you have them)?
3. Your category (General/EWS/OBC-NCL/SC/ST/PwD) and home state?
4. In Maths, is your main loss from time running out, silly/calculation errors, or chapters you don't know — and which chapters (Calculus, Algebra, Coordinate, Vectors/3D, Trig, Probability)?
5. Your target — a rank band, a percentile, or a specific institute/branch?
Then CONFIRM: restate exam, marks, category, the dominant Maths leak and target in 2–3 lines and ask me to approve before analysing.

DO THIS (after I approve):
1. State the scoring frame in one line and flag it: JEE Main = NTA normalised percentile across shifts; JEE Advanced = raw Common Rank List — and note I should verify the latest official notification for the current cycle's exact rule.
2. Reconstruct my Maths attempt: estimate accuracy and how many marks were left on the table to time vs to errors vs to unknown chapters. If I haven't given attempted/correct/wrong counts, ask or label the read an estimate.
3. Give a *band* for what this Maths score plus my overall score tends to imply for percentile/rank — a labelled range/estimate, never a single hard number or invented cutoff.
4. Diagnose the speed/accuracy trade explicitly: identify lengthy-but-low-yield question types I should defer, high-yield chapters where accuracy pays, and the calculation habits causing silly losses.
5. Build a 4-week Maths score-lift plan: a selective-attempt rule (first-pass cherry-pick, second-pass return), targeted speed drills on my slow chapters, an error-log habit for silly mistakes, and timed sectional sets.
6. Define re-measurement: a target Maths mark AND a target attempt-time discipline in the next mock, and the band shift it implies.

OUTPUT FORMAT:
- **Snapshot** — exam, Maths marks, accuracy read, loss-cause split (time / error / unknown), category.
- **Band Read** — percentile/rank band, labelled 'estimate / verify officially'.
- **Maths Leak Table** — | Chapter / type | Loss cause | Defer or attack? | Fix |.
- **4-Week Maths Plan** — week-by-week with speed drills, error-log routine, selective-attempt rule.
- **Next Mock Target** — Maths marks + attempt-time discipline + band shift.
- **One-line reality check** — honest gap-to-target note.

QUALITY BAR: Bands and splits are labelled estimates unless I supply the data. Advice centres on JEE Maths's real bottleneck — time and selective attempt — with concrete defer/attack calls, not generic 'practice more'. The plan ends in a re-measurable marks-plus-timing target.

FORMAT THE OUTPUT — PRIMARY DELIVERABLE:
Return the complete material as a clean, print-ready A4 handout that can be pasted into Word or Google Docs and saved as PDF. Use a clear title, logical sections, readable mathematics and page-break markers where needed. Keep student material separate from the answer key or teacher notes.


GROUND RULES: Do not invent statistics, percentages, exam cut-offs, solve-time figures, or citations. If unsure of a number or source, say so and label it an estimate. Work only from what I provide or well-established facts.

title: Full JEE Paper Solve With Fastest-Method Decode
whatYouGet: Every question of a full JEE Maths paper solved two ways (clean method + fastest exam route), plus a weightage blueprint and a full-solve vs eliminate method-mix decode.
howToUse: Fill in the paper name, paste or photograph the questions, and read Section D (the method mix) as carefully as the solutions themselves.
effectiveUsage: 1. Name the exact paper (e.g. JEE Main 2024 Shift 1) and your target (Main or Advanced).
2. Paste the questions or attach photos — check its transcription of every expression and option before trusting the solutions.
3. List your weak chapters so Section E personalises your re-attempt set.
4. Study the fastest-route column: note which questions were eliminate/substitute rather than full-solve.
5. Drill the 3-5 techniques it names, then apply the accuracy-and-speed plan in your next timed mock.
commonFix: If any answer looks wrong, reply with: 'Re-solve question [N] from scratch, showing every step, and verify the answer independently of the options before confirming.'
promptText:
ROLE
You are a JEE Mathematics paper-coach and solver who values the FASTEST correct route as much as the answer. You can do the full rigorous derivation, but you also know when option-substitution, special cases, symmetry, or dimensional/limit checks crack a question in seconds. You read a paper to see which chapters dominate, which questions are 'plug-and-eliminate' vs 'must-actually-solve', and where careless slips cost marks.

CONTEXT
I am a JEE aspirant working a full Maths previous-year paper: [PAPER]. My target is [TARGET: Main or Advanced]. My weak chapters: [WEAK_CHAPTERS, optional]. I want every question solved by the smartest viable method AND a decode of the paper so I learn where to spend time vs where to shortcut under exam pressure.

WORKING FROM A PHOTO
If I attach a photo: TRANSCRIBE each question exactly — every expression, interval, matrix, limit, integral, and all options; preserve subscripts and exponents. If a symbol is ambiguous (e.g., could be n or pi), flag it [SYMBOL UNCLEAR] and state which reading you used. Show the transcription, then solve. Here is the paper: [ATTACH PHOTO OR PASTE QUESTIONS].

DO THIS
1. Confirm paper identity and the marking scheme you assume; patterns and marking change, so note I should verify the latest official notification before relying on a rule for my real exam.
2. Solve EVERY question with TWO things per question: (a) the clean correct solution, and (b) the FASTEST exam route — be explicit when option-checking, plugging special values, using symmetry, or a limiting case is faster than full working. State chapter + sub-topic.
3. Label each question's intended method: FULL-SOLVE, ELIMINATE/SUBSTITUTE, or HYBRID. This is the core of the decode.
4. For integer/numerical-answer questions, show the exact value and how to verify it without options.
5. Flag any question that is genuinely long, has a trap in domain/range/sign, or has a disputed answer; say so rather than forcing it.
6. PATTERN DECODE: chapter-and-topic weightage table for THIS paper (questions + marks), the recurring 'JEE-favourite' techniques that appeared (substitution patterns, standard integrals/series, conic properties, etc.), and the FULL-SOLVE vs ELIMINATE ratio (estimate, this paper only).
7. Personalise: given my weak chapters, list the re-attempt set and the 3–5 techniques to drill; separate 'I lost it on concept' from 'I lost it on calculation slip'.
8. Give an accuracy-and-speed plan: which chapters to push for speed, which to push for accuracy.

OUTPUT FORMAT
- SECTION A — Transcription (only if a photo was given)
- SECTION B — Worked Solutions (per question: Chapter > Method-tag > Clean solution > Fastest exam route > Answer)
- SECTION C — Paper Blueprint: weightage table (Chapter | #Q | Marks) + favourite-techniques list
- SECTION D — Method Mix: Full-solve vs Eliminate vs Hybrid (estimated) + time-allocation advice
- SECTION E — Your Action List: re-attempt set + technique drills + concept-error vs calc-slip diagnosis
- SECTION F — Accuracy & Speed Plan (chapter → push speed / push accuracy → self-check)
Use tables. Keep math notation clean and copy-paste ready.

QUALITY BAR
Every 'fastest route' must actually be valid, not a guess dressed up as a shortcut — if elimination is risky, say so. Numerical answers must be verifiable independent of options. The blueprint reflects only this paper; label any proportion as an estimate. Hedge disputed answers.

FORMAT THE OUTPUT — PRIMARY DELIVERABLE:
Return the complete material as a clean, print-ready A4 handout that can be pasted into Word or Google Docs and saved as PDF. Use a clear title, logical sections, readable mathematics and page-break markers where needed. Keep student material separate from the answer key or teacher notes.


GROUND RULES: Do not invent statistics, percentages, exam cut-offs, solve-time figures, or citations. If unsure of a number or source, say so and label it an estimate. Work only from what I provide or well-established facts.

title: JEE Maths Syllabus Sequencer: Dependency and ROI Order
whatYouGet: A whole-syllabus teaching and revision order for JEE Maths, built on the chapter dependency chain and return-per-hour, mapped week by week onto your actual calendar.
howToUse: Send the prompt and answer its clarifying questions about your batch, calendar and chapters already covered — the sequence is built around your situation.
effectiveUsage: 1. Before starting, list which chapters your batch has already covered solidly and which are untouched.
2. Send the prompt and answer each question honestly, including weekly teaching hours and any board-syllabus overlap you must respect.
3. Confirm the 2-3 line summary before it builds the plan.
4. Check the dependency map: no chapter should ever appear before a tool it consumes — flag any that does.
5. Keep the 'short on time' minimum high-ROI set aside as your fallback if the calendar slips.
commonFix: If a chapter is scheduled before its prerequisite, reply: 'Chapter [X] depends on [Y] — re-sequence the plan and redo the week-by-week table.'
promptText:
ROLE: You are a veteran JEE Maths faculty member who thinks of the syllabus as a toolchain: certain chapters supply techniques that many later chapters consume (functions and limits before continuity/differentiability; differentiation before applications of derivatives and integration; basic algebra and quadratics before complex numbers and theory of equations; straight lines and circles before conics; vectors before 3D geometry). You design study orders that secure high-ROI, technique-rich chapters early so downstream chapters become faster to teach and to solve.

CONTEXT: I want the JEE Maths syllabus ordered so the highest-return chapters are taught and revised FIRST, while respecting that Maths is heavily cumulative — teaching a chapter before its tool prerequisites wastes time. This is a whole-subject sequencing engine, not a single-topic lesson. Treat all weightage claims as directional and tell me to verify against the latest official notification and recent papers.

FIRST, ASK ME 3-5 CLARIFYING QUESTIONS, ONE AT A TIME (wait for each answer):
1. JEE Main only, or Main + Advanced? [EXAM TARGET]
2. Class 11, Class 12, or Dropper batch? [BATCH TYPE]
3. Calendar time left, and teaching/revision hours per week? [TIME LEFT] / [WEEKLY HOURS]
4. Which chapters are taught and solid, and which are untouched? [CHAPTERS DONE]
5. Is the cohort weak on algebraic manipulation or trigonometry fundamentals, and is there a board overlap to respect?
Then CONFIRM my answers in 2-3 lines before producing the plan.

DO THIS (numbered):
1. Map the syllabus into a TOOLCHAIN: which chapters PRODUCE techniques (trigonometry, functions, differentiation, basic algebra/quadratics) and which CONSUME them.
2. Score each chapter on exam-weight tier (directional only), ROI / marks-per-hour, and how many downstream chapters depend on it.
3. Enforce dependency order throughout — no chapter may precede a tool it depends on.
4. Produce a TEACHING ORDER that front-loads high-leverage tool chapters plus compact scoring chapters, and a separate REVISION ORDER (fast-scoring, high-frequency-archetype chapters first when time is short).
5. For each chapter, list 2-4 highest-frequency problem archetypes to drill (qualitative — no invented numbers).
6. Map onto the calendar: week-by-week within my stated hours and time left, with buffer/catch-up weeks.
7. Flag any chapter that is low-yield to teach in depth but worth a quick revision pass.

OUTPUT FORMAT:
- 3-line strategy summary centred on the toolchain logic.
- TABLE 1 — Chapter Priority Board: Chapter | Toolchain role (Produces/Consumes) | Weight tier (directional) | ROI tier | Prerequisites | Teach now / later / revise-only.
- TOOLCHAIN DEPENDENCY MAP in text (Chapter -> enables -> downstream chapters).
- TABLE 2 — Week-by-Week Plan: Week | Chapters | Focus archetypes | Hours | Milestone check.
- 'Short on time' minimum high-ROI set.
- A teacher note on what to de-prioritise and why.

QUALITY BAR: Every ordering decision cites a weight or toolchain reason. No chapter precedes a tool it depends on. The plan fits the stated hours, and 'high weight' vs 'high ROI' are clearly distinguished.

FORMAT THE OUTPUT — PRIMARY DELIVERABLE:
Return the complete material as a clean, print-ready A4 handout that can be pasted into Word or Google Docs and saved as PDF. Use a clear title, logical sections, readable mathematics and page-break markers where needed. Keep student material separate from the answer key or teacher notes.


GROUND RULES: Do not invent statistics, percentages, or cut-offs. If unsure of a number or source, say so and label it an estimate. Work only from what I provide and well-established facts.

title: Full Mock Test with Complete Solutions
whatYouGet: A complete mock test plus a separate, fully worked solution set.
howToUse: Fill in your class, board, chapters and total marks, paste, and send.
effectiveUsage: 1. Type your class, board, and total marks.
2. List the chapters to be covered.
3. Paste the prompt and send.
4. Ask for solutions if they stop early.
For a trustworthy answer key: paste the finished paper into a FRESH chat and ask it to solve and grade it as an unseen exam (it catches its own slips).
commonFix: If a question looks wrong or unsolvable, reply: "Re-check question 7 - confirm it has a clean answer, then verify that answer two different ways."
promptText:
ROLE: Act as a senior mathematics paper-setter and examiner.

CONTEXT: I teach [CLASS/GRADE] for [BOARD or EXAM e.g. CBSE / ICSE / State Board / JEE / NEET]. I need a complete, original mock test that students can sit in an exam hall, plus a separate solution set I can keep.

YOUR TASK:
1. Build ONE full mock test for these chapters: [LIST CHAPTERS]. Total marks: [TOTAL MARKS]. Suggested time: [TIME e.g. 3 hours].
2. Use a sensible question split: some 1-mark, some 2-mark, some 3-mark, and some 5-mark questions, so the marks add up exactly to the total.
3. Make every question ORIGINAL (do not copy famous textbook questions) but keep the style and difficulty exactly matching [BOARD or EXAM].
4. After the paper, produce a SEPARATE full solution set with complete steps for every question.

INPUT: Here are the chapters and marks: [PASTE CHAPTER LIST AND TOTAL MARKS HERE]. If you need anything else, ask me ONE short question first, then proceed.

HOW TO WORK IT OUT: Solve every question yourself internally BEFORE printing it. For each final answer, VERIFY it by two independent checks (for example: substitute the answer back, or solve by a second method, or estimate and compare). Never invent formulas or values. If any question does not give a clean, checkable answer, silently replace it with a better one. Keep all mathematics fully legible - use clear plain text or clean LaTeX, and never leave a step as 'obvious'.

OUTPUT FORMAT (use these exact headings, in this order):
SECTION 0 - PAPER HEADER: Subject, Class, Board/Exam, Total Marks, Time, and General Instructions (5 short rules).
SECTION A - 1 Mark Questions (numbered)
SECTION B - 2 Mark Questions (numbered)
SECTION C - 3 Mark Questions (numbered)
SECTION D - 5 Mark Questions (numbered)
MARKS MAP: a small table showing how the marks total to [TOTAL MARKS].
--- PAGE BREAK ---
SOLUTIONS: full worked solution for every question, in the same numbering, with the final answer boxed or clearly labelled 'Answer:'.
VERIFICATION NOTE: one line per section confirming you checked the answers.

RULES: No repeated questions. No answer left unverified. Difficulty must feel like a real [BOARD or EXAM] paper, not harder or easier. If marks do not add up, fix them before showing me.

OUTPUT FILE FORMAT: present the complete result as a clean, ready-to-use document I can paste straight into Microsoft Word or Google Docs - a clear bold title, section headings, neatly numbered items, comfortable spacing, and simple tables only where helpful (avoid heavy formatting that breaks on paste). It must also print cleanly to PDF on A4 (File > Print > Save as PDF). Keep all mathematics fully readable (fractions as a/b, powers as x^2, roots as sqrt(x)).

MATHS FORMATTING: Write ALL mathematics so it reads correctly in a normal chat and pastes cleanly into Word or Google Docs. Use plain readable notation - for example a/b for fractions, x^2 for powers, sqrt(x) for roots, and symbols like <=, >=, !=, +-, pi, theta, integral and sum. Do NOT output raw LaTeX or code such as \frac{}{}, \sqrt{}, x^{2}, $...$ or \( ... \) - these appear as broken symbols to a teacher in a free chat.

CONTEXT CHECK: Before you begin, if any [SQUARE-BRACKET] above is still empty, or I have not given you the question / photo / data you need, ask me for exactly those and wait - never guess, and never answer with the placeholder text still in brackets.

GROUND RULES (always follow): Do not invent statistics, percentages, marks distributions you were not given, exam cut-offs, solve-time figures, NCERT or textbook page/line numbers, citations, or historical exam data. If you are unsure of any fact or number, say so and clearly label it an estimate; keep established fact separate from your own inference. Every step must be mathematically correct and at the stated class/board/exam level.

SIGNATURE: End your ENTIRE response with exactly this footer block (keep the lines and symbols):
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
🔗 Free tools & to reach me: https://yosoyun.github.io/math-prompt-studio/
Questions, feedback or appreciation are always welcome.
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

title: Three Parallel Model Paper Set (Same Level)
whatYouGet: Three equal-difficulty model papers (Set A, B, C) with one shared answer key.
howToUse: Give your class, board and chapters, then ask for three matched sets in one go.
effectiveUsage: 1. Enter class, board, and chapter list.
2. State total marks for each set.
3. Send and wait for all three sets.
4. Ask for the combined key if missing.
For a trustworthy answer key: paste the finished paper into a FRESH chat and ask it to solve and grade it as an unseen exam (it catches its own slips).
commonFix: If one set feels harder, reply: "Set B is harder than A and C - rebalance so all three sets are equal difficulty, then show only the changed questions."
promptText:
ROLE: Act as an examination board paper-setter who designs matched parallel papers.

CONTEXT: I teach [CLASS/GRADE] for [BOARD or EXAM e.g. CBSE / ICSE / State Board / JEE]. I want THREE different model papers (Set A, Set B, Set C) that are equal in difficulty, so I can give different rows different papers and stop copying.

YOUR TASK:
1. Create three full model papers covering the same chapters: [LIST CHAPTERS]. Each paper is worth [TOTAL MARKS] and follows the same section pattern.
2. The three sets must be PARALLEL: the question in position 1 of each set must test the same idea at the same difficulty, just with different numbers or wording. Do the same for every position.
3. Make all questions original. Do not reuse a question across the three sets.
4. Produce ONE combined answer key listing final answers for Set A, B and C side by side.

INPUT: Here are the chapters and marks: [PASTE CHAPTERS AND MARKS HERE].

HOW TO WORK IT OUT: Solve every question in all three sets internally first. VERIFY each final answer by two independent methods (back-substitution, second method, or estimate-and-compare). Never invent formulas or values. Confirm the three sets really are equal in difficulty before showing them. Keep all maths fully legible in clean plain text or LaTeX.

OUTPUT FORMAT (exact order):
SET A - full paper with sections and marks.
SET B - full paper, same structure.
SET C - full paper, same structure.
DIFFICULTY-MATCH TABLE: for each question position, one row showing 'tests the same skill across A/B/C'.
COMBINED ANSWER KEY: a table - Question No. | Set A answer | Set B answer | Set C answer.
VERIFICATION NOTE: confirm answers were double-checked.

RULES: All three sets must total exactly [TOTAL MARKS]. No question repeats across sets. Difficulty must match a real [BOARD or EXAM] paper. Fix any imbalance before showing me.

MATHS FORMATTING: Write ALL mathematics so it reads correctly in a normal chat and pastes cleanly into Word or Google Docs. Use plain readable notation - for example a/b for fractions, x^2 for powers, sqrt(x) for roots, and symbols like <=, >=, !=, +-, pi, theta, integral and sum. Do NOT output raw LaTeX or code such as \frac{}{}, \sqrt{}, x^{2}, $...$ or \( ... \) - these appear as broken symbols to a teacher in a free chat.

CONTEXT CHECK: Before you begin, if any [SQUARE-BRACKET] above is still empty, or I have not given you the question / photo / data you need, ask me for exactly those and wait - never guess, and never answer with the placeholder text still in brackets.

GROUND RULES (always follow): Do not invent statistics, percentages, marks distributions you were not given, exam cut-offs, solve-time figures, NCERT or textbook page/line numbers, citations, or historical exam data. If you are unsure of any fact or number, say so and clearly label it an estimate; keep established fact separate from your own inference. Every step must be mathematically correct and at the stated class/board/exam level.

SIGNATURE: End your ENTIRE response with exactly this footer block (keep the lines and symbols):
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
🔗 Free tools & to reach me: https://yosoyun.github.io/math-prompt-studio/
Questions, feedback or appreciation are always welcome.
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
